about: First-time win-rate bands for levels 1 to 5, per pillar and per bot, from the Advisor's targets. Hero stats are not nerfed to meet them. A figure that misses its band can only be listed in known_misses with its measured value: CI then fails if it gets worse or comes back inside its band.
measure: HoldfastCurve.climb: a first-time player who buys the cheapest star and gold nodes between runs, wears the gear found, places posts and replays a level until it wins. A rate is first-attempt wins over the players who reached the level. Bots: average (reacts in 6 ticks, special every decision), poor (18 ticks, special every second decision).

hard.about: First-attempt win rate of each level's Hard replay for the average bot, played once right after the level is first cleared (the same players as the climbs). The modifier changes how the level is played (faster, tougher or more dangerous monsters, a frailer Keep, leaner pay), so Hard is a different fight and not the same one with bigger numbers. The bands are the first measurement with room each way; the Advisor and the Head of Engineering set the final ones.

tree.how: the average bot plays on from the end of the tutorial, spending stars and gold between runs, playing each cleared level's Hard replay once and replaying its latest level; the hours are the play time until it owns every gold node its Hero can reach (the whole budget if it never does), and a dry run is a return to the tree with nothing affordable. No wait for a purchase may pass 6 runs (the dearest node alone is allowed that long, Advisor view 17 Nov 2026) and the median wait before a purchase is at most 2, so the first hour stays quick. The stars the five levels pay cannot fill the tree, so the star side is reported, not judged, until more levels exist.

pillar_levels_note: Which levels each pillar is judged on (a pillar not named is judged on all five). The Dusk Mage unlocks at the level 5 boss and the Tideblade at the next biome boss, so both are tuned to the biomes they unlock into (Advisor view 2026-10-30, Head of Engineering decision). Gull Rock, the hardest level that exists, stands in for them. WIDEN THE SCOPE when a later biome exists. The gate fails if a pillar's scope is empty. Levels outside a scope are reported as not played by that pillar yet.
pillar_ceilings_note: A pillar's own ceiling for the average bot's first-time win rate, in place of the level's when higher (Advisor view 17 Nov 2026, Head of Engineering decision): the Dusk Mage unlocks after the level 5 boss and is meant to be strong late in the dark, so a pillar a little easier than the starter does no harm, and Gull Rock is shared by every pillar so it is not hardened for it. Re-check when a second biome exists; if the extra ease shows at a second level, trim the Dusk Mage's own numbers. A Dusk Mage attack buff was measured and left out: it makes an idle Dusk Mage win Shingle Beach, which the no-input guard tests forbid.

fork_gap.how: per level and pillar, the first-time win rate of the Volley side against the Sniper side (average bot, 12 players each)

special_gap.how: per pillar, the first-time win rate of the average bot with its special less the same players with it never pressed; the mean over the levels judged is at most 40 points (the special is worth pressing, not required), and the first level is winnable without it

one_post.how: the Dusk Mage with only the first castle slot bought, average bot, 12 players

known_misses_note: A pinned miss may not get worse, and CI fails if it comes back inside its band (delete the pin then). Build 16 (HF-M2-28) emptied the list of everything that could be fixed without breaking another rule. What was fixed: the Tideblade's basic attack is stronger (damage 9 to 10, health 80 to 86, nothing nerfed), which lifts what it wins without its special (the special is worth 33 points or less, its poor play and Hard replay are in band); the Dusk Mage's Gull Rock rate gets its own ceiling (pillar_ceilings) instead of a harder Gull Rock, as the Advisor ruled; the fork feel is judged from the level where fork nodes are owned (owned_share) with a check that the first fork comes within 3 runs of Tidewrack Cove; the wait for a purchase may be 6 runs for the dearest node with a median of 2 or fewer, so the dry-run pins are gone. What remains: flare_archer/no_special/outpost, 0% against 30%. Making the Outpost easier for the bot that never presses the special (thinner waves) also lets a run with NO input win it (nine of nine), and the guard tests (a run with no input is lost on the first two levels; a plain bot loses at least once on every level) forbid that, because the idle Hero and Keep win before the moving bot does; no Hero or pack number can lift the one without the other, so the guarded rule wins and the guided first press (HF-M2-63) is what teaches the button before that fight. The three tree/hours pins (HF-M2-68): the gold nodes are priced from the gold a run pays where each tier opens (content/base/gold_tiers.json), so the average bot owns every gold node its Hero can reach in about an hour of play against the 3 to 4 hours the Advisor sets for the whole tree; the Advisor reads real play at about 2 to 2.5 hours (a bot buys better and never hesitates), asks to re-check in the Gate 2 tester sessions, and not to change prices or structure before that.

fork_feel.owned_share_note: Judged from the first level where the average bot has bought a fork node in at least this share of its runs, so it moves by itself if the pacing changes (Advisor view 17 Nov 2026). The first fork is not meant to be affordable at Shingle Beach: it comes within reach around level 3 after two or three saving runs, both sides shown on the card.
fork_feel.how: per level and pillar, the larger of the gap in Keep health left (a share of full health) and in clear time (a share of the longer one) between the Volley side and the Sniper side, first attempts of the average bot: the two sides must feel different even where they win as often

fork_reach.how: the first fork node is owned within this many runs of reaching Tidewrack Cove (mean of the fork players, the Flare Archer's sides saving up for it): a player who picks a side must not wait long for it
